issues.detail: The Greek 'τα παντα' (all things/everything) is omitted. The Vietnamese translates it as 'một' (one), which changes the scope from 'all things' to a single unit.

The Greek phrase 'εἰ δε ην' implies a conditional hypothetical ('if [it] were not'). The Vietnamese 'Nếu chỉ có' (If there only were) captures the condition but loses the specific contrastive negation/hypothetical structure of 'δε ην'.
